title: Appliance Repair Follow-Up Visit Checklist Form
subtitle: Control diagnosis, repair, maintenance, testing, and return to use through verified identity, domain-specific observations, evidence, authorization, exception ownership, and accountable closeout.
description: An original, workflow-complete appliance repair follow-up visit checklist for appliances and utility connections. It connects manufacturer service information, approved scope, and customer authorization to present conditions, repeatable evidence, decisions, unresolved work, and the receiving party's handoff.
use_case: Use when a qualified appliance service technician must compare a current appliance repair condition with prior service evidence, decide whether it is planned, recurring, incomplete, or new, and assign the next action.

sections.title: Appliance Repair follow-up access, safety, and evidence readiness
sections.guidance: Confirm present conditions independently; a prior completion record does not establish that the current condition is safe.

blocks.label: Present access, isolation, protection, and work controls
items: Electrical supply isolated and verified before exposed work
Gas, water, steam, or other utility isolated when required
Stored heat, pressure, motion, and sharp-part exposure controlled
Floor, cabinetry, contents, and adjacent finishes protected
Refrigerant work routed to an appropriately certified technician
Replacement part compatibility verified before installation
Recall or manufacturer service notice checked when applicable
Customer kept from operating the appliance during controlled work
Leak, combustion, and ventilation concerns receive a stop-work response
Restoration test plan defined before utilities are reconnected

sections.title: Appliance Repair targeted reinspection and comparison
sections.guidance: Compare like-for-like conditions where possible and distinguish a recurrence from a new or unrelated condition.

blocks.label: Appliance Repair condition and service points rechecked
items: Power cord, plug, receptacle, disconnect, and visible wiring condition
Gas or fuel connection, shutoff, ignition, flame, and venting condition
Water supply, inlet, drain, hose, seal, and leak condition
Refrigerant circuit, tubing, coils, condensate, and airflow condition
Door, latch, hinge, gasket, interlock, and enclosure condition
Motor, fan, pump, belt, bearing, and other moving-part condition
Control panel, sensor, thermostat, display, and error history
Heating, cooling, washing, drying, or cycle performance
Mounting, leveling, clearances, anchorage, and anti-tip provisions
Safety devices, guards, labels, and required warnings

blocks.label: Prior-to-current finding and evidence comparison
Repeat measurement, method, and comparison log
blocks.guidance: Applicable concepts include: Supply voltage or electrical reading, Operating current or resistance, Temperature rise, drop, or setpoint, Pressure, vacuum, or leak-test result, Cycle time, flow, or drain performance, Level, clearance, airflow, or vibration observation.

sections.guidance: Close only when outcome, remaining limitation, next action, evidence, and receiving ownership agree.

blocks.guidance: This appliance repair follow-up visit checklist is an operational record, not a substitute for applicable law, licensing, product labeling, manufacturer instructions, site policy, safety requirements, or professional judgment. Stop affected work, access, application, operation, testing, or release when electrical, gas, refrigerant, water, combustion, structural, recall, or other unsafe condition is unresolved. A qualified appliance service or safety supervisor must review the exception, authorize the controlling decision, and preserve its evidence before closeout.
